items.q: Myocardial necrosis after total occlusion spreads in which direction?
items.exp: The subendocardium is most vulnerable (highest wall stress, lowest perfusion), so necrosis begins there and wavefronts outward over hours. This creates the reperfusion salvage window.
r: Incorrect. The inner wall dies first, not last.
Correct. Necrosis wavefronts from subendocardium outward.
Incorrect. Layers die sequentially, not simultaneously.
Incorrect. Territory follows the occluded artery, not apex alone.
items.kp: Inner wall first: subendocardium is the most vulnerable layer.

items.q: Free wall rupture and tamponade most likely occur when after transmural infarction?
o: Three to seven days when macrophages soften the wall
After scar matures at three months
items.exp: Macrophage clearance at three to seven days maximally weakens necrotic wall before collagen forms, peaking rupture of free wall, septum and papillary muscle. Early and late periods are stronger.
r: Incorrect. Minutes old necrosis retains structural strength.
Correct. Days three to seven are the rupture window.
Incorrect. Mature scar resists rupture but may aneurysm.
Incorrect. Rupture follows wall weakening, not reperfusion itself.
items.kp: Rupture peaks when macrophages have eaten the wall: days 3 to 7.

items.q: Contraction band necrosis in an infarct indicates what has occurred?
items.exp: Reperfused dead myocytes flood with calcium and hypercontract into dense contraction bands, the histological signature of reperfusion. Unreperfused infarcts show plain coagulative necrosis instead.
r: Incorrect. Collaterals limit infarct size without bands.
Correct. Contraction bands mark reperfusion injury.
Incorrect. Calcium deposits in scars and valves differently.
Incorrect. Amyloid stiffens walls without infarct bands.
items.kp: Bands mean blood returned to already dead muscle.

items.q: Anterior wall and septal infarction follows occlusion of which artery?
items.exp: The left anterior descending artery supplies the anterior left ventricular wall, anterior septum and apex, so its occlusion causes the largest and most dangerous infarcts with conduction risk.
r: Incorrect. Right coronary supplies inferior wall and often the nodes.
Correct. LAD supplies anterior wall and septum.
Incorrect. Circumflex supplies lateral wall.
Incorrect. Posterior descending supplies inferior septum as part of RCA or circumflex systems.
items.kp: Anterior infarct equals LAD culprit until proven otherwise.

items.q: Sudden new holosystolic murmur with pulmonary oedema four days after infarction suggests what?
o: Papillary muscle rupture with acute mitral regurgitation
items.exp: Papillary muscle necrosis and rupture floods the left atrium through acute severe mitral regurgitation, causing pulmonary oedema with a new murmur. Septal rupture adds a shunt with right sided signs.
r: Incorrect. Free wall rupture causes tamponade and collapse, not this murmur.
Correct. Papillary rupture causes torrential mitral regurgitation.
Incorrect. Aneurysm forms weeks later without acute murmur.
Incorrect. A rub is pericarditis, without regurgitant murmur.
items.kp: Post infarct murmur plus lung flooding: papillary muscle has snapped.

items.q: Troponin rise after severe sepsis with tachycardia and hypotension but no plaque event is classified how?
o: Type 2 infarction from supply demand mismatch
items.exp: Type 2 infarction is necrosis from oxygen supply demand imbalance (hypotension, tachycardia, hypoxia) without acute plaque disruption. Management treats the underlying stressor and evaluates coronary disease separately.
r: Incorrect. Type 1 requires plaque disruption with thrombosis.
Correct. Demand mismatch necrosis is type 2 infarction.
Incorrect. Myocarditis is inflammation needing different evidence.
Incorrect. Unstable angina has ischaemia without necrosis or troponin rise.
items.kp: Troponin plus supply crisis without plaque event equals type 2.

items.q: The earliest histological change of infarction (first hours) is what?
o: Wavy fibres with early coagulative necrosis
items.exp: Border zone myocytes stretch into wavy fibres within hours with early coagulative change, before neutrophils flood in at one to three days. Scarring takes weeks.
r: Incorrect. Neutrophils peak at one to three days.
Correct. Wavy fibres are earliest.
Incorrect. Collagen scar needs weeks to mature.
Incorrect. Hemosiderin marks old haemorrhage organisation.
items.kp: Hours: wavy fibres. Days: neutrophils. Weeks: scar.

items.q: A thinned dyskinetic scar bulging outward months after infarction with mural thrombus is what?
items.exp: True aneurysm is full thickness thinned scar that bulges paradoxically, harbouring mural thrombus and arrhythmia but rarely rupturing. Pseudoaneurysm is a contained rupture with narrow neck needing urgent repair.
r: Incorrect. Pseudoaneurysm is contained rupture, narrow necked and dangerous.
Correct. Scarred bulging wall is a true aneurysm.
Incorrect. Diverticulum is congenital and contractile.
Incorrect. Fibroelastoma is a small valvular tumour.
items.kp: True aneurysm rarely ruptures; pseudoaneurysm must be repaired.

items.q: First presentation of coronary disease is most tragically which event in many patients?
o: Sudden cardiac death from ventricular arrhythmia
items.exp: Sudden arrhythmic death during acute ischaemia or over scar is the first manifestation in a substantial minority, which is why risk factor prevention precedes symptoms in importance.
r: Incorrect. Angina is common but not the tragic first event meant.
Correct. Sudden death is often the first presentation.
Incorrect. Failure develops later in survivors.
Incorrect. Incidental findings are benign presentations by contrast.
items.kp: Coronary disease may announce itself with sudden death.

items.q: Hibernating myocardium is best defined as what?
o: Chronically hypoperfused viable muscle with reduced contraction that recovers after revascularisation
items.exp: Hibernating myocardium downregulates contraction under chronic low flow but stays viable, recovering after bypass or stenting. Scar cannot recover, separating the two on viability imaging.
r: Incorrect. Scar is dead and cannot recover function.
Correct. Viable downregulated muscle that recovers is hibernating.
Incorrect. Bands mark reperfusion necrosis, not chronic adaptation.
Incorrect. Athletic hypertrophy is physiological growth.
items.kp: Hibernating means asleep but alive: revascularise to wake it.
